Thanks Priyom — I reviewed Draft_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx and left tracked changes. Summary of legal position:

1) Pen-test notifications: we can accept a 48-hour notice only for non-intrusive/remote vulnerability scans and agreed-upon staging endpoints. For live/targeted active exploitation tests that could impact service availability our standard remains 72 hours and a pre-test approval conversation.

2) Remediation windows: propose the following carve-outs in the exhibit:
   - Critical vulnerabilities: initial remediation plan required within 7 calendar days; if a hotfix cannot be implemented, agree interim mitigation and weekly status updates until closure.
   - High/Medium: 30 calendar days to remediation with reasonable exceptions for complex third-party issues.

3) Audit rights / SOC 2: we will provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II and a SOC 2 letter of attestation. We cannot provide raw control evidence or unrestricted access to internal logs; we can establish a secure evidence handoff process and a 30-day evidence request turn around for reasonable queries during contracting.

4) Escalation & confidentiality: added a clause that requires any security findings shared during procurement to be marked "Confidential — for remediation coordination only" and prohibits external distribution.

I've attached the redline file name "Draft_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx" with comments and included suggested paragraph text below for easy copy/paste into your procurement template. If Cerulean agrees to the non-intrusive carve for 48 hours we'll accept that in writing; otherwise default to 72 hours for live tests.

Suggested exhibit snippet (insert into section 3.2 - Penetration Testing):
"Vendor shall provide notice to Customer at least seventy-two (72) hours prior to any active penetration test targeting Redwood production infrastructure, except that remote vulnerability scans or other non-intrusive assessments aimed only at pre-authorized staging endpoints may occur with at least forty-eight (48) hours' prior notice, provided such activity is conducted under a mutually-agreed rules of engagement (ROE)."

I'll await Cerulean's response; happy to hop on a short call with Anita if they'd like to go line-by-line.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Hi all — thanks for the quick turn, Laura. We appreciate the carve on non-intrusive scans. Two quick items from our procurement/legal side:

1) Can we get the 48-hour clause to cover both staging and production if the tests are low-impact (tool-based scans, no exploitation)? Our supplier program has standardized templates that expect 48 hours across the board; making an exception to production would require internal sign-off which will delay the contract.

2) On SOC 2 evidence: redacted report + letter are fine. We do ask for an annual confirmation from vendors that there have been no material changes since the last SOC 2 period; would Redwood be willing to provide a short attestation statement at renewal?

If you can accept 48 hours for low-impact production scans with an agreed ROE and provide a renewal attestation, we can circulate a procurement-ready order form and move to DocuSign.

Cheers,
